paper_title: Epistemic Boundaries and Quantum Uncertainty: What Local Observers Can (Not) Predict
statement: Can post-quantum theories have predictive advantage whilst conforming to the Born rule on average? We showed that unless epistemic boundaries exist between observers, the answer is no: quantum uncertainty is an unavoidable limit to Nature’s predictability. For any hypothetical predictive advantage, there exists a quantum measurement scenario with a finite number of settings which implies that predictive advantage would violate no-signalling. Giving up the assumption of ‘reliable intersubjectivity’ does in principle enable (subjective) predictive advantage (and even knowledge about the outcomes of non-commuting observables), but implies an epistemic boundary between different quantum observers.
